_scope: ONE node, ONE function: `matchesLocation` inside `Map Candidate Fields`. No change to any score or threshold, no change to query generation, no change to phase 2, no change to the loop, the completion guard or billing.

_theDefect.reportedAs: a Baghdad search delivered candidates located in Egypt and Switzerland
_theDefect.measuredIn: exec 2035 (HR Business Partner, 2026-09-29): of the 4 candidates scoring >= 50, the delivered three were located `IQ`, `Cairo, EG` and `CH`.
_theDefect.rootCause: `matchesLocation` decides residence from `allProfileLocationText()` — a blob that concatenates city, state, country, headline, occupation, summary AND every past experience's location, title, company and description. `hasIraqTerm(blob)` therefore returns true for anyone who has EVER mentioned Iraq anywhere in their profile, so a Cairo-based candidate with one past Iraqi job passes the location test. `currentLocationText()` already exists and is already computed, but is used only in a soft-pass branch — never as the deciding signal.
_theDefect.secondRootCause: City names are treated as proof of country. Production returned `"Erbil, SY"` — an Iraqi city with a SYRIAN country code — and `IRAQ_TERMS` contains `erbil`, so it was accepted as Iraqi. Any allowlist built from city names repeats this bug; the ISO country code has to win.

_whyNotTheDownstreamCopies: `isBadLocation` is copy-pasted into `Sort By Match Score`, `Finalize Top N Send` and `Finalize Phase 2 Send` with a SHORTER exclude list than this node's (theirs omits cairo, istanbul, riyadh, amman, beirut, bahrain, oman, pakistan, india, bangladesh). They are a cruder second pass over the already-mapped `location` string. Once `matchesLocation` drops a non-Iraqi profile via `__skip`, those copies never see it, so they are left untouched here — fixing them is cosmetic and would widen the blast radius for no measured gain. Recorded so the duplication is not forgotten.

_measuredGroundTruth.source: all 47 rows of head_hunter_candidates in production, 2026-09-29
_measuredGroundTruth.note: every single one carries a trailing ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code, and none has an empty location — so a country-code rule is decisive in practice, not theoretical

_expectedEffect: FEWER candidates, deliberately. Replayed against the two real searches: exec 2036 is UNCHANGED (2 delivered — all its >=50 candidates are genuinely in Iraq), exec 2035 goes 3 -> 1 because Cairo and Switzerland are correctly removed. This fix improves precision and does NOT raise the count; raising the count is the separate query-design work.
_openDecisionForTheOwner: `Finalize Top N Send` and `Finalize Phase 2 Send` wrap their location clean in `if (cleaned.length > 0) shortlist = cleaned;` — so when a filter would empty the shortlist it is SKIPPED and the foreign candidates are delivered anyway. This patch does not touch that. Because this patch drops non-Iraqi profiles much earlier (at `__skip`), the pool reaching that fallback is already clean, so the fallback becomes unreachable for location reasons. Stated explicitly so nobody later reads the fallback as still protecting anything.
_lineEndings: The live jsCode arrived with CRLF. It is PUBLISHED WITH LF, deliberately: the value has to be transmitted as a JSON string and hand-escaping 315 CRLF pairs is a real transcription risk, while the line ending has no effect on the JavaScript. In the repo the whole jsCode is one JSON string on one line, so the diff is a single line either way. The applier therefore normalises to LF and the byte-match check is made against that LF form.
